salient_findings: Diffuse extraoral swelling over the right cheek
Solitary, mobile, submucosal mass on the right buccal mucosa
key_facts: 30-year-old woman
2-month history of swelling in the right cheek
Severe pain associated with the swelling
Diffuse extraoral swelling over the right cheek
Solitary, mobile, 2 cm × 2 cm submucosal mass
Mass located on the right buccal mucosa
Smooth mucosal surface without color change
Ultrasonography showed a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical description of a mobile, submucosal mass with a smooth surface

shortlist.label: Ectopic lymph node
shortlist.why_kept: Considered in differential diagnosis based on clinical and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a swelling with a smooth mucosal surface

shortlist.label: Salivary gland tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Could present as a submucosal mass in the cheek region

shortlist.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Less common but plausible cause of a jaw or cheek swelling

raw.rationale: The presence of severe pain and a mobile submucosal mass with ill-defined borders are more consistent with an ectopic lymph node, which can be painful and have varying degrees of mobility

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically painless and have well-defined borders

rejected.label: Mucocele
rejected.why: Mucoceles usually present with a fluctuant, painless mass and are often associated with a history of trauma or salivary gland obstruction

rejected.label: Salivary gland tumor
rejected.why: Salivary gland tumors can be painful but are less likely to be mobile and have ill-defined borders

rejected.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Keratocystic odontogenic tumors are typically associated with the jaw and have a distinct radiographic appearance
